event: Scrabble tiles spilling onto the game board/table, interpreted as a 'splashing sound' in the context of a spill.

sounding_object.description: Wooden Scrabble tiles (approx. 10-20 of them) spilling from a red/purple cardboard Scrabble game box lid. The tiles are small, light tan colored wooden squares, approximately 2cm x 2cm. The box lid is rectangular cardboard, part of the game packaging. The spill is caused by the man sitting to the right of the camera wearer.

reference_object.description: The camera worn by the first-person participant.

facing_object.object_name: The man and the Scrabble board area
facing_object.description: The camera wearer is generally facing the Scrabble board on the table and the man sitting to their right, who is interacting with the game pieces at the time of the spill.

question: Imagine you are the camera wearer, when the splashing sound comes up, relative to where you are facing, where is the sound source: left, right, or back? If the object is generally to your left and facing it requires turning less than 120 degrees left, choose 'left'. If the object is generally to your right and facing it requires turning less than 120 degrees right, choose 'right'. If the object is generally behind you and facing it requires turning 120 degrees or more, choose 'back'.
